Last Friday (the 21st), in the ruling of the Hong Kong Alliance case, in the early hours, police took a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing into a police vehicle and removed her. The police replied to enquiries that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or deliberately obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent".

Last Friday around 5 a.m., more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue "was suspected of wearing a top with somewhat seditious intent", and took her into a police vehicle and left. When officers took the woman away, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and pulled the orange cordon line toward the direction of Ying Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon line. On that day, a "court-watching enthusiast" queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese text printed on it.

The Collective Reporting Society (集誌社) enquired with the police about the reasons for taking the woman away and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (the 24th) that on August 21, a security operation was conducted in the area around West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts, during which a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or deliberately obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent", and was detained for investigation.
